text:
mia: heads up — saw a flurry of scale events in eu-west this morning, pods ending up stuck in Terminating for minutes after node scale-in. looks like lifecycle/CSI detach race when CA and machine-controller both act.
aj: got logs?
mia: pastes: 
```
I0323 07:12:14 node-controller: Starting delete for node ip-10-0-4-77
W0323 07:12:15 kubelet: failed to detach volume: device busy
I0323 07:12:18 cluster-autoscaler: removing node ip-10-0-4-77 (no recently started pods)
```

lucas: hunch — our terraform/helm automation sometimes flips taints/labels on nodepool right as CA decides to scale. if machine object terminates before pods finish preStop, CSI detach fails and drains hang.
kai: are these spot nodes or on-demand?
mia: mostly spot gpu pools. eviction -> quick termination. we have preStop hooks on long-running inference pods but they rely on kubelet window.
ops-bot: deploybot: helm release gpu-nodepool-autoscaler updated by ci-cd at 2026-03-15T07:11:58Z
oncall-sre: pinging @aj and @lucas — this is a customer-impact risk if inference jobs get stuck and cause retry storms.
aj: quick mitigation: add a short preDrain annotation on GPU jobs to extend terminationGracePeriodSeconds and annotate CA so it delays scale-down if annotation present. also plan to add a small on-demand buffer pool.
lucas: +1. we should also change terraform module to set lifecycle.create_before_destroy = true for nodepool resource to avoid momentary label/taint flips during replace. snippet: 
```hcl
resource "cloud_node_pool" "gpu" {
  name = var.name
  preemptible = true
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}
```

kai: for helm/autoscaler values, propose toggling `scaleDownDelayAfterAdd` and `maxEmptyBulkDelete` to reduce aggressive deletes. example values: 
```yaml
clusterAutoscaler:
  enabled: true
  extraArgs:
    scale-down-delay-after-add: 10m
    max-empty-bulk-delete: 1
```

mia: that seems reasonable. what about node termination notification handling? can we ensure the cloud provider webhook labels node with termination timestamp so CA knows to avoid removing it?
aj: we already have provider termination-notice but it's not wired into our drain hook. I'll add a small controller to annotate `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: true` during the grace window on nodes with pending termination signals.
oncall-sre: log note — please make the controller emit an event so ops can filter.
lucas: will update the terraform module to create the on-demand buffer pool (2 nodes) and expose a variable for size. also add a helm value to set the drain timeout for gpu workloads.
mia: ok i'll open two PRs: 1) helm values change + CA arg tweaks, 2) terraform change for create_before_destroy + buffer pool. i'll run canary in eu-west1 first.
aj: test plan: simulate spot eviction, confirm pods gracefully terminate within new windows, and CA does not prematurely delete. add an integration test that runs kubelet detach scenario.
kai: minor: add metric for drain-duration so we can alert if > 2m for GPU pods.
oncall-sre: noted. tagging oncall for tomorrow: @oncall-sre will watch the canary. :eyes:
mia: thanks team. will link PRs here when ready. :thumbsup:
